title: The Tube Gains a Second Floor

scenes.tts: Graft a second notochord against the side of a chick neural tube. The neural cells beside it start to behave like floor plate.
scenes.visual: Title card: The Tube Gains a Second Floor. A tube cross-section with a grafted rod pressed to its side wall; the wall beside it glows like the floor.
scenes.narration: Graft a second notochord against the side of a chick neural tube. The neural cells beside it start to behave like floor plate.

scenes.tts: The tube gains a second bottom. So how does a cell in the wall know how far it sits from the bottom?
scenes.visual: Two glowing floors on one tube. A single wall cell is highlighted with a question mark beside it.
scenes.narration: The tube gains a second bottom. So how does a cell in the wall know how far it sits from the bottom?

scenes.tts: Its neighbours tell it. A cell's position is written in how much signal it receives from below and above.
scenes.visual: Arrows enter the tube from a rod below and from the skin above; two opposing colour fades cross the wall, gold from below and blue from above.
scenes.narration: Its neighbours tell it. A cell's position is written in how much signal it receives from below and above.

scenes.tts: Start with the map. The neural tube rolls up from the neural plate and becomes the brain and spinal cord.
scenes.visual: A flat sheet of ectoderm rolls up into a hollow tube, which is then sliced crosswise. Labels: neural plate, neural tube, dorsal at top.
scenes.narration: Start with the map. The neural tube rolls up from the neural plate and becomes the brain and spinal cord.

scenes.tts: Under the tube runs the notochord, a rod of mesoderm, the embryo's middle cell layer.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. The notochord is drawn in and labelled.
scenes.narration: Under the tube runs the notochord, a rod of mesoderm, the embryo's middle cell layer.

scenes.tts: The tube's bottom strip is the floor plate, a narrow line of specialized cells. Its top strip is the roof plate.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. The floor plate and roof plate are highlighted and labelled.
scenes.narration: The tube's bottom strip is the floor plate, a narrow line of specialized cells. Its top strip is the roof plate.

scenes.tts: The epidermis, the non-neural ectoderm, ends up over the top of the tube.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. The epidermis is drawn over the top and labelled.
scenes.narration: The epidermis, the non-neural ectoderm, ends up over the top of the tube.

scenes.tts: In the wall between floor and roof, dividing cells called progenitors line the central canal.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. Progenitors in the ventricular zone are highlighted and labelled.
scenes.narration: In the wall between floor and roof, dividing cells called progenitors line the central canal.

scenes.tts: They will make motor neurons near the bottom, and relay neurons for body sensation near the top.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. Motor neuron icons appear near the bottom; sensory relay neuron icons near the top.
scenes.narration: They will make motor neurons near the bottom, and relay neurons for body sensation near the top.

scenes.tts: The ventral half of the wall will hold five stripes of progenitors, called domains. Each makes one class of neuron.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. Five empty stripes appear in the ventral wall, labelled p0, p1, p2, pMN and p3 from top to bottom, each with a blank tag.
scenes.narration: The ventral half of the wall will hold five stripes of progenitors, called domains. Each makes one class of neuron.

scenes.tts: The map raises four puzzles. Who marks the bottom? What is the signal? How is a slope read? How does a slope become lines?
scenes.visual: Four numbered boxes under the map: who marks the bottom; what is the signal; how is a slope read; how does a slope become lines.
scenes.narration: The map raises four puzzles. Who marks the bottom? What is the signal? How is a slope read? How does a slope become lines?

scenes.tts: Start with the first. Notochord and floor plate touch and share features. Is that a shared history, or an instruction?
scenes.visual: Zoom to the notochord and floor plate touching. Box 1 is highlighted. Two captions: shared history? or instruction?
scenes.narration: Start with the first. Notochord and floor plate touch and share features. Is that a shared history, or an instruction?

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety, Marysia Placzek, with Thomas Jessell, Jane Dodd and colleagues, ran the test in chick embryos.
scenes.caption: In 1990, Marysia Placzek, with Thomas Jessell, Jane Dodd and colleagues, ran the test in chick embryos.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Placzek, Tessier-Lavigne, Yamada, Jessell and Dodd, 1990. A chick embryo in an opened egg.
scenes.narration: In 1990, Marysia Placzek, with Thomas Jessell, Jane Dodd and colleagues, ran the test in chick embryos.

scenes.tts: A notochord grafted beside the side wall gave the nearby neural cells floor-plate properties.
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. A second notochord is grafted at the side wall; the cells it touches turn floor-plate colour. Label: graft.
scenes.narration: A notochord grafted beside the side wall gave the nearby neural cells floor-plate properties.

scenes.tts: Now the reverse. Predict: what happens at the midline if you remove the normal notochord early?
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. The normal notochord is lifted away. Question on screen: remove it early. What happens at the midline?
scenes.narration: Now the reverse. Predict: what happens at the midline if you remove the normal notochord early?

scenes.tts: Floor-plate properties failed to appear at the midline.
scenes.visual: The midline stays plain, with no floor-plate colour. Label: notochord removed, no floor plate.
scenes.narration: Floor-plate properties failed to appear at the midline.

scenes.tts: The graft shows the notochord is sufficient. It is enough to give floor-plate properties in a new place.
scenes.visual: Definition card: sufficient, enough to give the effect in a new place. The graft image beside it.
scenes.narration: The graft shows the notochord is sufficient. It is enough to give floor-plate properties in a new place.

scenes.tts: The removal shows it is necessary. Without it, the normal floor plate does not form.
scenes.visual: Definition card: necessary, no normal floor plate without it. The removal image beside it.
scenes.narration: The removal shows it is necessary. Without it, the normal floor plate does not form.

scenes.tts: Then the floor plate passes the message on. In culture, floor plate induced floor-plate markers, just as notochord did.
scenes.visual: Credit: Placzek, Jessell and Dodd, 1993. A dish with neural plate tissue placed against floor plate; the tissue lights up with floor-plate markers.
scenes.narration: Then the floor plate passes the message on. In culture, floor plate induced floor-plate markers, just as notochord did.

scenes.tts: The signals acted by contact. In this homeogenetic induction, an induced tissue recruits its neighbours to the same identity.
scenes.visual: The words homeogenetic induction on screen. Floor plate colour spreads from one cell to its neighbours, one row at a time.
scenes.narration: The signals acted by contact. In this homeogenetic induction, an induced tissue recruits its neighbours to the same identity.

scenes.tts: Keep one idea in view through every chapter. The neighbours supply a slope. The progenitors draw the lines.
scenes.visual: Rule card: the neighbours supply a slope; the progenitors draw the lines.
scenes.narration: Keep one idea in view through every chapter. The neighbours supply a slope. The progenitors draw the lines.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: in these assays, the bottom of the tube is told, and once told, it recruits. Something passes from the notochord. What is it?
scenes.visual: The transverse neural tube map, dorsal up: notochord below, floor plate at the bottom, ventricular zone around the central canal, roof plate at the top, epidermis over it. Box 1 fills with: told, then recruits. An arrow from the notochord carries a question mark. Takeaway on screen.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: in these assays, the bottom of the tube is told, and once told, it recruits. Something passes from the notochord. What is it?
